paper.title: Do Not Trust The Auctioneer: Learning to Bid in Feedback-Manipulated Auctions

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated first-price auctions with max-shilling feedback (known shill distribution)
unmapped: First-price auction: bid p_t in [0,1] given observed value v_t, reward (v_t-p_t)1{p_t>=b_t}
After a loss the learner observes o_t = max(b_t, s_t), where s_t is an independent shill bid (feedback-only manipulation)
Shill-bid distribution F_S is known to the learner
Values, competing bids and shill bids are i.i.d. from V, B, S on [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: At round \(t\), the learner observes a value \(v_t\in[0,1]\), chooses a bid \(p_t\in[0,1]\) and competes against the highest real competing bid \(b_t\). The learner wins if \(p_t\ge b_t\), receives reward \(v_t-p_t\), and otherwise receives reward \(0\) and observes the shilled report \(o_t=\max\{b_t,s_t\}\), where \(s_t\) is a shill bid.

algorithms.name: Robust/optimistic interval elimination with dyadic shill-scale validation (Algorithm known_FS)

symbols.rho: number of disjoint active bid regions covering the active intervals at every epoch
symbols.gamma: lower bound on F_S over active regions (probability of informative low-shill events)

conditions: Assumption 1 (weak RHR condition on buyer distribution B)
active intervals covered by at most rho active bid regions at every epoch
F_S is (gamma, C_S)-regular on each region (Assumption 2)

source.label: thm:upper-bound
source.quote: Assume \cref{ass:weak-rhr-buyer} and suppose that \(F_S\) is known to the learner. If, at every epoch, the active intervals maintained by the optimistic branch can be covered by at most \(\rho\) active bid regions, and \(F_S\) is \((\gamma,C_S)\)-regular on each such region ..., then the algorithm satisfies R_T \le \widetilde O(\min\{T^{2/3},\rho^{1/4}\sqrt T\,\gamma^{-1/4}\}).

results.notes: Regret is expectation of utility differences against the best bid for the realized value (pseudo-regret). Theorem also states rho=1 special case min{T^{2/3}, sqrt(T) gamma^{-1/4}} (not recorded separately). Feedback mapped to partial_monitoring as censored win/loss plus shilled report.

conditions: Assumption 1 (weak RHR condition on buyer distribution B)
no regularity condition on F_S required

source.label: thm:upper-bound
source.quote: If the regularity condition fails on the intervals considered by the optimistic branch, or if the optimistic certificate does not validate, the same algorithm falls back to the robust branch and still guarantees \(R_T\le \widetilde O(T^{2/3})\).

results.notes: Fallback robust guarantee in the same theorem.

symbols.gamma: value of F_S on the hard bid interval J (probability of informative low-shill events)

conditions: F_S(q) = gamma for every q on the hard interval J
holds even if the learner knows F_S

source.label: th:single-region-lower-bound
source.quote: Fix $ T\ge 1$ and $ \gamma\in(0,1]$. There is a constant $ c>0$ such that, for every learning algorithm $ \pi$, there is an oblivious max-shilling instance satisfying \cref{ass:weak-rhr-buyer} and satisfying $F_S(q) = \gamma$ for every $q$ on a hard bid interval $J$, for which R_T(\pi) \ge c \min\brc{ T^{2/3}, \sqrt T\,\gamma^{-1/4}}.

results.notes: Hard instance uses fixed value v=1. Corollary 2 states minimax optimality up to logs for rho=1.
